slot.brief: Diagram of a wheel rolling without slipping; relate speed of a marked point on the rim to translational speed, or find acceleration of the contact point.

stem: A wheel of radius $1$ m rolls without slipping to the right. At the instant shown, its centre has speed $\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$ and acceleration $1$ m s$^{-2}$ to the right. The magnitude of the acceleration of point $P$, as shown in the figure, is

verdicts.working: For rolling without slipping, \(\omega=\sqrt2\) clockwise and \(\alpha=1\) clockwise. At the top point, tangential acceleration is \(1\) right and centripetal acceleration is \(2\) downward. Including the centre’s \(1\) rightward acceleration gives \(\vec a_P=(2,-2)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), so \(|\vec a_P|=2\sqrt2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

working:
For rolling right, $\vec{\omega}=-(v_C/R)\hat{k}$ and $\vec{\alpha}=-(a_C/R)\hat{k}$. At the top, $\vec{a}_P=\vec{a}_C+\vec{\alpha}\times(R\hat{j})-\omega^2R\hat{j}=2a_C\hat{i}-(v_C^2/R)\hat{j}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}$ m s$^{-2}$. Thus $|\vec{a}_P|=2\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-2}$.

Independent check: For rolling without slipping, \(\omega=\sqrt2\) clockwise and \(\alpha=1\) clockwise. At the top point, tangential acceleration is \(1\) right and centripetal acceleration is \(2\) downward. Including the centre’s \(1\) rightward acceleration gives \(\vec a_P=(2,-2)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), so \(|\vec a_P|=2\sqrt2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

draft.stem: A wheel of radius $1$ m rolls without slipping to the right. At the instant shown, its centre has speed $\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$ and acceleration $1$ m s$^{-2}$ to the right. The magnitude of the acceleration of point $P$, as shown in the figure, is

figure.description: Draw a circle representing a wheel tangent to a horizontal ground line. Mark its centre C and the point P at the very top of the rim. Draw a radius from C to P and label it $R=1$ m. At C, draw two separate horizontal arrows pointing right; label them $v_C=\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $a_C=1$ m s$^{-2}$.

draft.working: For rolling right, $\vec{\omega}=-(v_C/R)\hat{k}$ and $\vec{\alpha}=-(a_C/R)\hat{k}$. At the top, $\vec{a}_P=\vec{a}_C+\vec{\alpha}\times(R\hat{j})-\omega^2R\hat{j}=2a_C\hat{i}-(v_C^2/R)\hat{j}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}$ m s$^{-2}$. Thus $|\vec{a}_P|=2\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-2}$.
draft.distractor_notes: A: Omits the centripetal acceleration component. B: Omits the tangential acceleration due to angular acceleration. D: Adds the component magnitudes instead of combining them vectorially.
